chunk_findings.detail: The new sentence tells the reader that a PATCH-only skew "is not refused: the write goes through with a one-time warning", with no exception named, and this transcript is the golden for the user-facing `config --explain` text. But the change's own intent states the opposite for one command: "an older adopt is refused even for a patch". Concrete failure: a machine on ddflow 0.1.9 against a log last written by 0.1.10 (same minor, same data format level, no capability gap) with `[upgrade].skew = "refuse"` runs `ddflow adopt`; per the intended behaviour that write is refused with exit 3, yet the paragraph this change just wrote into the knob doc (and regenerated the golden for) says such a write "goes through with a one-time warning", because the carve-out is stated over *every* write ("asked to WRITE"), not just the ones that honour it. A doc-update change whose stated purpose is "docs left stale by fix-B63635ddc6a" that documents the patch carve-out while leaving the adopt carve-out out of the same paragraph reproduces exactly the staleness it set out to fix; the text needs to scope the sentence (e.g. "for commands other than adopt") or name the adopt refusal alongside it.
